assessment.nobel_worthiness: A precise cancellation of optical light shifts creates a powerful and conceptually clean atomic probe of time and gravity.
assessment.attribution: Katori's invention and Ye's precision development support an unusually focused attribution.
assessment.maturity: Lattice clocks have a substantial independent experimental record.
uncertainties: The packet alone does not establish the systematic uncertainty or priority of each specific milestone.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum control of macroscopic motion directly challenges the apparent boundary between quantum systems and ordinary mechanical objects.
assessment.attribution: The selected trio represents complementary mechanical, optical and circuit-control routes.
assessment.maturity: The basic preparation and control of mechanical quantum states is established experimentally.
uncertainties: A common citation must identify the decisive quantum-control contributions and fairly reconcile the different routes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Building a many-body Hamiltonian from controlled atoms makes quantum correlations and phase transitions accessible to quantitative experiment.
assessment.attribution: Zoller represents the proposal; Bloch and Greiner represent decisive realization and microscopic exploration.
assessment.maturity: Optical-lattice quantum simulation is mature and widely reproduced.
uncertainties: The short entry cannot resolve the full history of enabling experimental and theoretical contributions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Squeezed light shows that quantum fluctuations are controllable and that precision limits depend on the physical state of the probe.
assessment.attribution: The proposed names cover the measurement principle, foundational optical demonstration and precision-interferometry development.
assessment.maturity: The phenomenon and measurement benefit have extensive experimental confirmation.
uncertainties: Review which implementations establish the claimed advance and the scope of a three-person citation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Trapped-ion logic links an explicit theoretical architecture with controlled entanglement of individual atoms, a clear advance in understanding and manipulating quantum systems.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller supply the proposal; Blatt represents sustained experimental realization.
assessment.maturity: The underlying quantum-control achievements have a long, independent record.
uncertainties: The original breakthrough should be distinguished from subsequent processor and error-correction milestones.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Matter-wave interferometry turns coherent atomic motion into precise tests of recoil, forces and fundamental physics.
assessment.attribution: The three names cover foundational photon-recoil, grating and light-pulse contributions.
assessment.maturity: The methods are established and independently used.
uncertainties: A contribution review should separate first realizations from later gains in sensitivity.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum phase records geometry and potentials even when a classical force account is insufficient. This is a profound conceptual change with observable consequences.
assessment.attribution: The two credited scientists correspond to the distinct phase discoveries in the entry.
assessment.maturity: Both effects are firmly established across quantum experiments.
uncertainties: The combined title needs a coherent citation that preserves the difference between the two contributions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: High-harmonic emission and lightwave control in solids open electronic motion inside crystals to strong-field interrogation on its natural time scale.
assessment.attribution: Ghimire and Reis represent the solid-state harmonic discovery; Huber represents complementary lightwave electron-control work.
assessment.maturity: The phenomena have developed beyond initial observation, but microscopic interpretation is more system-dependent than the title conveys.
uncertainties: Interband and intraband contributions, independent confirmation and the breadth of the bundled citation need careful review.
My expertise in atomic strong-field physics does not by itself settle solid-state attribution.
